sentences.text: The known fossil record of Diplognathus consists only of incomplete fragments of jaws and skulls.
Diplognathus mirabilis is considered fairly large, with lower jaws reaching up to 45 centimeters in length.
Diplognathus larfargei was much smaller than D. mirabilis, with lower jaws averaging about 4 centimeters in length.
The genus Diplognathus was first described by Newberry in 1878.
Fossils of Diplognathus have been found in the Cleveland Shale of Ohio, dating to the Late Devonian.
Evidence suggests that Diplognathus were large-eyed fish-eaters with weak but widely gaping jaws.
Diplognathus is classified within the class Placodermi.
Diplognathus belongs to the parent group Arthrodira.
In 1967, Obruchev classified the genus Diplognathus within the family Hadrosteidae.
It is debated whether Diplognathus belongs in Hadrosteidae, as Denison contested this placement in 1978 and preferred to classify it as Arthrodira incertae sedis.
Diplognathus lived during the Late Famennian stage of the Devonian period.
